3	This is the single state document of the continuous research loop.
4	Every cycle reads it first and updates it last. Keep it honest, keep
5	it current, keep it short — history goes to `archive/`, results go to
6	`experiments/` and `novel/`.
7	
8	## Goal
9	
10	An O(polylog) algorithm computing the n-th prime p(n) (equivalently
11	π(x)) exactly. Target: p(10^100) in < 1 s, 100% accurate.
12	
13	**Honest position:** every known computation route is blocked — 730+
14	approaches catalogued in `status/CLOSED_PATHS.md`, four obstruction
15	theorems, the information-theoretic barrier (~√x zeta-zero phases,
16	GUE-random, behind the last ~50% of digits). The goal may require
17	mathematics that does not exist. The deliverable of each cycle is
18	honest progress: working algorithms/protocols, new structural facts
19	with measurements, precisely-closed questions with mechanisms,
20	adjacent-problem wins. Never a faked breakthrough.
21

# PROGRAM.md — the live research program

This is the single state document of the continuous research loop.
Every cycle reads it first and updates it last. Keep it honest, keep
it current, keep it short — history goes to `archive/`, results go to
`experiments/` and `novel/`.

## Goal

An O(polylog) algorithm computing the n-th prime p(n) (equivalently
π(x)) exactly. Target: p(10^100) in < 1 s, 100% accurate.

**Honest position:** every known computation route is blocked — 730+
approaches catalogued in `status/CLOSED_PATHS.md`, four obstruction
theorems, the information-theoretic barrier (~√x zeta-zero phases,
GUE-random, behind the last ~50% of digits). The goal may require
mathematics that does not exist. The deliverable of each cycle is
honest progress: working algorithms/protocols, new structural facts
with measurements, precisely-closed questions with mechanisms,
adjacent-problem wins. Never a faked breakthrough.

## ACTIVE LINE — the verification program (started S491, 2026-06-13)

- Field-size-free commitment — the RS `N≤q` demo artifact removed (S514): built the

  behind the SAME `commit/prove/verify` interface in
  `experiments/constructions/p12_sumcheck_pi_verification/pcs_commit.py`, gated by a
  `code=` selector (`"rs"` default = every prior artifact verbatim; `"expander"`).
  Construction (Spielman/Druk–Ishai recursive, as in Brakedown): systematic
  `Enc_n(x)=x‖Enc_{⌈n/2⌉}(A·x)‖B·Enc_{⌈n/2⌉}(A·x)` with **column-regular** sparse A,B
  over F_q (coldeg=4) + a dense base case; the matrices are a fixed PUBLIC map (seed +
  size → q-free column indices, values mod q), so prover-commit and verifier-reencode
  build the identical linear code. The tensor reduction `S~(pt)=a^T M b` and the
  homomorphic column check `⟨a,Mhat[:,c]⟩=Enc(v)[c]` hold for ANY linear Enc, so the
  `O(t(r+k))=O(x^{1/4})` verifier is unchanged — the verifier re-encodes v,w ONCE
  (`O(N)=O(k)`, linear-time) then indexes the t queried columns. **Column-regularity is
  load-bearing:** a plain low-density generator leaves some input column unused → a
  weight-1 basis codeword → the forge cheat at that coordinate is uncatchable; making

8	S519 proved the transfer-matrix route to the EXACT A_k is closed (state
9	space Theta(A_k)) and reduced A_k to a count over only the active primes
10	B(k) ~ rho*(k) ~ k/ln k:
11	
12	    A_k = #{ S subset allowed(k) : for every prime q in B(k), the occupied
13	            residues {o mod q : o in S} do NOT cover all of Z_q }.
14	
15	The remaining question is purely asymptotic: the conjecture
16	A_k = e^{(1+o(1)) pi(k)}, i.e. ln A_k / (k/ln k) -> 1.  This script
17	estimates that constant WITHOUT exact counting.
18	
19	THE IDEA (exact reformulation).  Put the uniform measure on subsets:
20	each allowed offset is included independently with probability 1/2.  Then
21	
22	    A_k = 2^N * P[ admissible ],   N = |allowed(k)| = phi(k),
23	
24	EXACTLY (every subset has probability 2^{-N}).  Let C_q = "S covers all
25	classes mod q" (an INCREASING event) and \bar C_q = "S misses a class
26	mod q" (DECREASING).  admissible = intersection over q in B(k) of \bar C_q.
27	
28	  * MARGINAL (independent within a prime).  Classes mod q partition the
29	    allowed offsets into disjoint groups of sizes n_{q,0..q-1}, so
30	        p_q := P[\bar C_q] = 1 - prod_j (1 - 2^{-n_{q,j}}),
31	    computed exactly from the class sizes (no transfer matrix).
32	
33	  * MEAN FIELD = product over q (independent-primes leading term).  The
34	    \bar C_q are DECREASING events, hence positively associated (FKG), so
35	        P[ intersection ] >= prod_q p_q   ==>   A_k >= 2^N prod_q p_q
36	    is a RIGOROUS LOWER BOUND.
37	
38	  * CLUSTER EXPANSION (the corrections = CRT overlaps).  For T subset
39	    B(k) let P_T = P[ intersection over q in T of \bar C_q ].  Mobius
40	    inversion of f(T) = ln P_T gives the connected cluster terms
41	        c_T = sum_{U subset T} (-1)^{|T|-|U|} ln P_U,
42	    and EXACTLY  ln P_B = sum_{T subset B, T != empty} c_T.
43	    Truncating at |T| <= r is the order-r cluster approximation (r=1 is
44	    the mean field).
45	
46	THE ENGINE (joint cover via nested inclusion-exclusion).  P_T needs the
47	joint cover probabilities P[ intersection_{q in S} C_q ] for S subset T.
48	These have a NESTED I-E form: pick the largest prime L in S as the
49	"product" prime and inclusion-exclude over the missed classes of the
50	smaller "head" primes,
51	
52	  P[cover all q in S] = sum_{(U_h subset Z_h)_h} (-1)^{sum|U_h|}
53	        2^{-(#offsets in any head-class U_h)} * prod_{w in Z_L}
54	        (1 - 2^{-n_w}),   n_w = #offsets with (mod L = w) and
55	        (mod h not in U_h for every head h).
56	
57	Cost = 2^{sum of the all-but-largest primes of S} -- TINY for the small
58	primes that dominate the entropy, and INDEPENDENT of k (it depends only
59	on the primes, not on N).  This is exact (validated bit-for-bit against
60	the S519 transfer matrix count_tm) and FEASIBLE at k = 128, 256 where
61	count_tm on the full B(k) (Theta(A_k) states, S519) is dead.
62	
63	WHY THIS BEATS THE FULL TRANSFER MATRIX.  count_tm on the full B(k) has
64	Theta(A_k) states.  A 3- or 4-prime cluster term needs only a 2^{O(small
65	primes)} I-E, so the r=3,4 cluster approximation is computable at k=128
66	(and k=256), validated against exact A_k for k <= 64.
67	
68	MEASURED (validation, clean family):
69	  - the mean field is always below exact (FKG holds);
70	  - the cluster errors ALTERNATE in sign and shrink ~5x per order
71	    (odd r under, even r over), so [r=3, r=2] empirically BRACKETS A_k;
72	  - r=3 is within <1% of ln A_k by k=64.
73	
74	What would falsify a result here:
75	  - the mean field exceeding exact A_k for any k (FKG/lower-bound bug);
76	  - the joint-cover I-E disagreeing with count_tm (selftest asserts
77	    bit-for-bit on pairs and triples over k=32,64);
78	  - the full cluster sum (r=|B|) NOT equalling ln A_k - N ln2 (Mobius
79	    identity bug) -- selftest asserts it;
80	  - the cluster truncation error NOT shrinking with r at validated k
81	    (then the expansion does not converge and the estimate is void --
82	    reported honestly, no extrapolation).
83	
84	Usage:
85	  python3 census_entropy_asymptotic.py --selftest
86	  python3 census_entropy_asymptotic.py --k 64               # detail one k
87	  python3 census_entropy_asymptotic.py --k 128 --rmax 4     # estimate A_128
88	  python3 census_entropy_asymptotic.py --scan 8 256 --rmax 4

108	# class sizes and the marginal p_q (exact, no transfer matrix)
109	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
110	def class_sizes(allowed, q):
111	    per = [0] * q
112	    for o in allowed:
113	        per[o % q] += 1
114	    return per

117	def marginal_lnp(allowed, q):
118	    """ln p_q = ln P[S misses a class mod q], p=1/2.
119	    p_q = 1 - prod_j (1 - 2^{-n_j}); computed via log1p/expm1 so we never
120	    subtract two near-equal floats for tiny p_q."""
121	    ln_cover = 0.0
122	    for n in class_sizes(allowed, q):
123	        ln_cover += math.log1p(-(2.0 ** (-n)))
124	    pq = -math.expm1(ln_cover)
125	    if pq <= 0.0:                              # cover==1 to float precision
126	        pq = sum(2.0 ** (-n) for n in class_sizes(allowed, q))
127	    return math.log(pq), pq

131	# joint cover probability via nested inclusion-exclusion (the engine)
132	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
133	def joint_cover_prob(allowed, S, cost_cap=None, memo=None):
134	    """P[ intersection_{q in S} C_q ] = P[cover every class mod q, all q
135	    in S] under the uniform (p=1/2) measure.
136	
137	    Nested I-E with the LARGEST prime as the product prime.  Cost =
138	    prod over head primes of 2^h = 2^{sum(S)-max(S)}.  Returns None if
139	    that exceeds cost_cap (caller treats the cluster as unavailable).
140	    S = [] -> 1.0 (empty cover).  `memo` (keyed by sorted-tuple) avoids
141	    recomputing the same joint cover (the costly large blocks recur in
142	    both the upper bound and the lower-bound partition)."""
143	    S = sorted(S)
144	    key = tuple(S)
145	    if memo is not None and key in memo:
146	        return memo[key]
147	    if not S:
148	        return 1.0
149	    heads, L = S[:-1], S[-1]
150	    leaves = 1
151	    for h in heads:
152	        leaves <<= h                            # 2^h
153	    if cost_cap is not None and leaves > cost_cap:
154	        if memo is not None:
155	            memo[key] = None
156	        return None
157	    no = len(allowed)
158	    # per-head per-residue offset bitmasks; per-L-class offset bitmasks
159	    head_cls = [[0] * h for h in heads]
160	    for i, o in enumerate(allowed):
161	        for hi, h in enumerate(heads):
162	            head_cls[hi][o % h] |= (1 << i)
163	    Lcls = [0] * L
164	    for i, o in enumerate(allowed):
165	        Lcls[o % L] |= (1 << i)
166	
167	    total = 0.0
168	    # recurse over head subsets, accumulating the excluded-offset bitmask
169	    def rec(hi, excl_mask, sign):
170	        nonlocal total
171	        if hi == len(heads):
172	            excl = excl_mask.bit_count()
173	            prod = 2.0 ** (-excl)
174	            for w in range(L):
175	                n_w = (Lcls[w] & ~excl_mask).bit_count()
176	                prod *= (1.0 - 2.0 ** (-n_w))
177	            total += sign * prod
178	            return
179	        cls = head_cls[hi]
180	        h = heads[hi]
181	        for U in range(1 << h):
182	            m = 0
183	            uu = U
184	            r = 0
185	            while uu:
186	                if uu & 1:
187	                    m |= cls[r]
188	                uu >>= 1
189	                r += 1
190	            s = -sign if (U.bit_count() & 1) else sign
191	            rec(hi + 1, excl_mask | m, s)
192	    rec(0, 0, 1)
193	    if memo is not None:
194	        memo[key] = total
195	    return total

198	def P_miss(allowed, T, cost_cap=None, memo=None):
199	    """P[ intersection_{q in T} \bar C_q ] (miss a class mod every q in T)
200	    = sum_{S subset T} (-1)^{|S|} P[cover all q in S].  None if any needed
201	    joint-cover term exceeds cost_cap."""
202	    tot = 0.0
203	    for r in range(len(T) + 1):
204	        for S in combinations(T, r):
205	            jc = joint_cover_prob(allowed, list(S), cost_cap, memo)
206	            if jc is None:
207	                return None
208	            tot += ((-1) ** r) * jc
209	    return tot

215	def ie_cost_log2(block):
216	    """log2 of the nested-I-E cost of a block = sum of all but the largest."""
217	    if len(block) <= 1:
218	        return 0
219	    return sum(block) - max(block)

222	def greedy_blocks(B, cost_cap):
223	    """Partition the active primes into consecutive blocks, each with I-E
224	    cost <= cost_cap, greedily packing the SMALLEST primes together (they
225	    carry the strongest correlations).  Coarser blocks => tighter FKG
226	    lower bound."""
227	    blocks, cur = [], []
228	    for q in B:
229	        if not cur:
230	            cur = [q]
231	            continue
232	        if (1 << ie_cost_log2(cur + [q])) <= cost_cap:
233	            cur.append(q)
234	        else:
235	            blocks.append(cur)
236	            cur = [q]
237	    if cur:
238	        blocks.append(cur)
239	    return blocks

242	def block_lower_bound(allowed, blocks, cost_cap, memo=None):
243	    """ln of the FKG block lower bound: A_k >= 2^N * prod_blocks P[miss
244	    within block].  Each block's joint-miss prob is exact (nested I-E).
245	    Returns (ln_lower, ok)."""
246	    N = len(allowed)
247	    tot = N * LN2
248	    for g in blocks:
249	        pm = P_miss(allowed, list(g), cost_cap, memo)
250	        if pm is None or pm <= 0.0:
251	            return None, False
252	        tot += math.log(pm)
253	    return tot, True

256	def best_single_block(B, cost_cap):
257	    """The largest prefix of B (smallest primes) whose single-block I-E is
258	    within the cap -- gives the tightest feasible UPPER bound
259	    2^N * P[miss within that block] >= A_k."""
260	    g = []
261	    for q in B:
262	        if (1 << ie_cost_log2(g + [q])) <= cost_cap:
263	            g.append(q)
264	        else:
265	            break
266	    return g

269	def cluster_term(T, lnP):
270	    """c_T = sum_{U subset T} (-1)^{|T|-|U|} ln P_U.  None if any ln P_U
271	    unavailable."""
272	    Tl = list(T)
273	    s = 0.0
274	    for r in range(len(Tl) + 1):
275	        for U in combinations(Tl, r):
276	            v = lnP.get(frozenset(U))
277	            if v is None:
278	                return None
279	            s += ((-1) ** (len(Tl) - r)) * v
280	    return s

283	def estimate(k, rmax=4, core_cut=None, cost_cap=1 << 20, max_states=6_000_000,
284	             want_exact=True):
285	    """Mean-field lower bound + cluster truncations r=1..rmax + rigorous
286	    count_tm upper bound + (if feasible) exact ln A_k.
287	
288	    core_cut: only cluster over active primes <= core_cut (larger active
289	    primes stay at mean-field order; justified because p_q ~ 1 there)."""
290	    allowed = allowed_offsets(k)
291	    enf = enforceable_primes(k, allowed)
292	    B, W, dropped = reduce_primes(k, allowed, enf)
293	    N = len(allowed)
294	    base = N * LN2
295	
296	    lnp, pq = {}, {}
297	    for q in B:
298	        lnp[q], pq[q] = marginal_lnp(allowed, q)
299	    mf_all = sum(lnp[q] for q in B)
300	    meanfield = base + mf_all                       # all-singletons FKG lower
301	
302	    memo = {}                                       # shared joint-cover cache
303	
304	    # rigorous FKG block lower bound (coarser partition => tighter)
305	    blocks = greedy_blocks(B, cost_cap)
306	    block_lower, _ = block_lower_bound(allowed, blocks, cost_cap, memo)
307	
308	    # rigorous single-block upper bound: 2^N P[miss within G] >= A_k
309	    Gup = best_single_block(B, cost_cap)
310	    pm_up = P_miss(allowed, Gup, cost_cap, memo)
311	    upper_ie = base + math.log(pm_up) if (pm_up and pm_up > 0) else None
312	
313	    core = list(B) if core_cut is None else [q for q in B if q <= core_cut]
314	
315	    # ln P_T for every subset of core with 1 <= |T| <= rmax (singletons are
316	    # the exact marginals; |T|>=2 via nested I-E)
317	    lnP = {frozenset(): 0.0}
318	    for q in core:
319	        lnP[frozenset((q,))] = lnp[q]
320	    skipped = []
321	    for r in range(2, min(rmax, len(core)) + 1):
322	        for T in combinations(core, r):
323	            pm = P_miss(allowed, list(T), cost_cap, memo)
324	            if pm is None or pm <= 0.0:
325	                lnP[frozenset(T)] = None
326	                skipped.append(tuple(T))
327	            else:
328	                lnP[frozenset(T)] = math.log(pm)
329	
330	    # cluster truncations
331	    trunc = {}
332	    cluster_contrib = {1: mf_all}
333	    for r in range(2, rmax + 1):
334	        if r > len(core):
335	            break
336	        s = 0.0
337	        for T in combinations(core, r):
338	            cT = cluster_term(T, lnP)
339	            if cT is not None:
340	                s += cT
341	        cluster_contrib[r] = s
342	    for rr in range(1, rmax + 1):
343	        tot = base
344	        for r in range(1, rr + 1):
345	            tot += cluster_contrib.get(r, 0.0)
346	        trunc[rr] = tot
347	
348	    # exact ln A_k via the S519 transfer matrix on the full active set, but
349	    # ONLY when it is feasible (small k) -- prefixes are nested so we climb
350	    # and stop at the first abort (never pays the slow full-B abort).
351	    exact = None
352	    if want_exact and N <= 40:                 # k <= 80: full B count_tm fits
353	        last = None
354	        for i in range(1, len(B) + 1):
355	            c, st = count_tm(k, list(B[:i]), allowed, max_states=max_states,
356	                             want_stats=True)
357	            if c is None:
358	                last = None
359	                break
360	            last = (math.log(c), B[:i])
361	        if last is not None and last[1] == B:
362	            exact = last[0]
363	
364	    return {
365	        "k": k, "N": N, "B": B, "W": W, "core": core, "base": base,
366	        "meanfield": meanfield, "block_lower": block_lower, "blocks": blocks,
367	        "upper": upper_ie, "upper_B": Gup, "trunc": trunc,
368	        "cluster_contrib": cluster_contrib, "exact": exact, "lnp": lnp,
369	        "pq": pq, "skipped": skipped,
370	    }

420	def _ls_slope(pts):
421	    n = len(pts)
422	    sx = sum(x for x, _ in pts)
423	    sy = sum(y for _, y in pts)
424	    sxx = sum(x * x for x, _ in pts)
425	    sxy = sum(x * y for x, y in pts)
426	    return (n * sxy - sx * sy) / (n * sxx - sx * sx)

476	def selftest():
477	    print("=== census_entropy_asymptotic selftest ===")
478	    n_ok = 0
479	
480	    # 1. marginal p_q (product) == count_tm({q})/2^N
481	    for k in (16, 32, 64):
482	        allowed = allowed_offsets(k)
483	        N = len(allowed)
484	        for q in enforceable_primes(k, allowed)[:4]:
485	            lp, p = marginal_lnp(allowed, q)
486	            lp_tm = math.log(count_tm(k, [q], allowed)) - N * LN2
487	            assert abs(lp - lp_tm) < 1e-9, (k, q, lp, lp_tm)
488	    n_ok += 1
489	    print("[1] marginal p_q (class-size product) == count_tm({q})/2^N")

491	    # 2. joint cover I-E == count_tm joint miss, bit-for-bit, pairs+triples
492	    for k in (32, 64):
493	        allowed = allowed_offsets(k)
494	        N = len(allowed)
495	        B, _, _ = reduce_primes(k, allowed)
496	        tests = [B[:2], B[:3]]
497	        if len(B) >= 5:
498	            tests += [list(B[2:5]), list(B[1:4])]
499	        for T in tests:

501	            tm = count_tm(k, list(T), allowed) / (2.0 ** N)
502	            assert abs(ie - tm) <= 1e-12 + 1e-9 * abs(tm), (k, T, ie, tm)
503	    n_ok += 1

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""census_entropy_asymptotic.py — the census entropy CONSTANT without
exact full enumeration, via a mean-field + cluster (Mayer/cumulant)
expansion.

Open item 4, PROGRAM.md NEXT ACTION (the part that survives S519).

S519 proved the transfer-matrix route to the EXACT A_k is closed (state
space Theta(A_k)) and reduced A_k to a count over only the active primes
B(k) ~ rho*(k) ~ k/ln k:

    A_k = #{ S subset allowed(k) : for every prime q in B(k), the occupied
            residues {o mod q : o in S} do NOT cover all of Z_q }.

The remaining question is purely asymptotic: the conjecture
A_k = e^{(1+o(1)) pi(k)}, i.e. ln A_k / (k/ln k) -> 1.  This script
estimates that constant WITHOUT exact counting.

THE IDEA (exact reformulation).  Put the uniform measure on subsets:
each allowed offset is included independently with probability 1/2.  Then

    A_k = 2^N * P[ admissible ],   N = |allowed(k)| = phi(k),

EXACTLY (every subset has probability 2^{-N}).  Let C_q = "S covers all
classes mod q" (an INCREASING event) and \bar C_q = "S misses a class
mod q" (DECREASING).  admissible = intersection over q in B(k) of \bar C_q.

  * MARGINAL (independent within a prime).  Classes mod q partition the
    allowed offsets into disjoint groups of sizes n_{q,0..q-1}, so
        p_q := P[\bar C_q] = 1 - prod_j (1 - 2^{-n_{q,j}}),
    computed exactly from the class sizes (no transfer matrix).

  * MEAN FIELD = product over q (independent-primes leading term).  The
    \bar C_q are DECREASING events, hence positively associated (FKG), so
        P[ intersection ] >= prod_q p_q   ==>   A_k >= 2^N prod_q p_q
    is a RIGOROUS LOWER BOUND.

  * CLUSTER EXPANSION (the corrections = CRT overlaps).  For T subset
    B(k) let P_T = P[ intersection over q in T of \bar C_q ].  Mobius
    inversion of f(T) = ln P_T gives the connected cluster terms
        c_T = sum_{U subset T} (-1)^{|T|-|U|} ln P_U,
    and EXACTLY  ln P_B = sum_{T subset B, T != empty} c_T.
    Truncating at |T| <= r is the order-r cluster approximation (r=1 is
    the mean field).

THE ENGINE (joint cover via nested inclusion-exclusion).  P_T needs the
joint cover probabilities P[ intersection_{q in S} C_q ] for S subset T.
These have a NESTED I-E form: pick the largest prime L in S as the
"product" prime and inclusion-exclude over the missed classes of the
smaller "head" primes,

  P[cover all q in S] = sum_{(U_h subset Z_h)_h} (-1)^{sum|U_h|}
        2^{-(#offsets in any head-class U_h)} * prod_{w in Z_L}
        (1 - 2^{-n_w}),   n_w = #offsets with (mod L = w) and
        (mod h not in U_h for every head h).

Cost = 2^{sum of the all-but-largest primes of S} -- TINY for the small
primes that dominate the entropy, and INDEPENDENT of k (it depends only
on the primes, not on N).  This is exact (validated bit-for-bit against
the S519 transfer matrix count_tm) and FEASIBLE at k = 128, 256 where
count_tm on the full B(k) (Theta(A_k) states, S519) is dead.

WHY THIS BEATS THE FULL TRANSFER MATRIX.  count_tm on the full B(k) has
Theta(A_k) states.  A 3- or 4-prime cluster term needs only a 2^{O(small
primes)} I-E, so the r=3,4 cluster approximation is computable at k=128
(and k=256), validated against exact A_k for k <= 64.

MEASURED (validation, clean family):
  - the mean field is always below exact (FKG holds);
  - the cluster errors ALTERNATE in sign and shrink ~5x per order
    (odd r under, even r over), so [r=3, r=2] empirically BRACKETS A_k;
  - r=3 is within <1% of ln A_k by k=64.

What would falsify a result here:
  - the mean field exceeding exact A_k for any k (FKG/lower-bound bug);
  - the joint-cover I-E disagreeing with count_tm (selftest asserts
    bit-for-bit on pairs and triples over k=32,64);
  - the full cluster sum (r=|B|) NOT equalling ln A_k - N ln2 (Mobius
    identity bug) -- selftest asserts it;
  - the cluster truncation error NOT shrinking with r at validated k
    (then the expansion does not converge and the estimate is void --
    reported honestly, no extrapolation).

Usage:
  python3 census_entropy_asymptotic.py --selftest
  python3 census_entropy_asymptotic.py --k 64               # detail one k
  python3 census_entropy_asymptotic.py --k 128 --rmax 4     # estimate A_128
  python3 census_entropy_asymptotic.py --scan 8 256 --rmax 4
"""

import argparse
import math
import os
import sys
import time
from itertools import combinations, product

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from census_transfer_matrix import (  # noqa: E402
    allowed_offsets, enforceable_primes, reduce_primes, count_tm,
    count_admissible_dfs, KNOWN,
)

LN2 = math.log(2.0)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# class sizes and the marginal p_q (exact, no transfer matrix)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
def class_sizes(allowed, q):
    per = [0] * q
    for o in allowed:
        per[o % q] += 1
    return per


def marginal_lnp(allowed, q):
    """ln p_q = ln P[S misses a class mod q], p=1/2.
    p_q = 1 - prod_j (1 - 2^{-n_j}); computed via log1p/expm1 so we never
    subtract two near-equal floats for tiny p_q."""
    ln_cover = 0.0
    for n in class_sizes(allowed, q):
        ln_cover += math.log1p(-(2.0 ** (-n)))
    pq = -math.expm1(ln_cover)
    if pq <= 0.0:                              # cover==1 to float precision
        pq = sum(2.0 ** (-n) for n in class_sizes(allowed, q))
    return math.log(pq), pq


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# joint cover probability via nested inclusion-exclusion (the engine)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
def joint_cover_prob(allowed, S, cost_cap=None, memo=None):
    """P[ intersection_{q in S} C_q ] = P[cover every class mod q, all q
    in S] under the uniform (p=1/2) measure.

    Nested I-E with the LARGEST prime as the product prime.  Cost =
    prod over head primes of 2^h = 2^{sum(S)-max(S)}.  Returns None if
    that exceeds cost_cap (caller treats the cluster as unavailable).
    S = [] -> 1.0 (empty cover).  `memo` (keyed by sorted-tuple) avoids
    recomputing the same joint cover (the costly large blocks recur in
    both the upper bound and the lower-bound partition)."""
    S = sorted(S)
    key = tuple(S)
    if memo is not None and key in memo:
        return memo[key]
    if not S:
        return 1.0
    heads, L = S[:-1], S[-1]
    leaves = 1
    for h in heads:
        leaves <<= h                            # 2^h
    if cost_cap is not None and leaves > cost_cap:
        if memo is not None:
            memo[key] = None
        return None
    no = len(allowed)
    # per-head per-residue offset bitmasks; per-L-class offset bitmasks
    head_cls = [[0] * h for h in heads]
    for i, o in enumerate(allowed):
        for hi, h in enumerate(heads):
            head_cls[hi][o % h] |= (1 << i)
    Lcls = [0] * L
    for i, o in enumerate(allowed):
        Lcls[o % L] |= (1 << i)

    total = 0.0
    # recurse over head subsets, accumulating the excluded-offset bitmask
    def rec(hi, excl_mask, sign):
        nonlocal total
        if hi == len(heads):
            excl = excl_mask.bit_count()
            prod = 2.0 ** (-excl)
            for w in range(L):
                n_w = (Lcls[w] & ~excl_mask).bit_count()
                prod *= (1.0 - 2.0 ** (-n_w))
            total += sign * prod
            return
        cls = head_cls[hi]
        h = heads[hi]
        for U in range(1 << h):
            m = 0
            uu = U
            r = 0
            while uu:
                if uu & 1:
                    m |= cls[r]
                uu >>= 1
                r += 1
            s = -sign if (U.bit_count() & 1) else sign
            rec(hi + 1, excl_mask | m, s)
    rec(0, 0, 1)
    if memo is not None:
        memo[key] = total
    return total


def P_miss(allowed, T, cost_cap=None, memo=None):
    """P[ intersection_{q in T} \bar C_q ] (miss a class mod every q in T)
    = sum_{S subset T} (-1)^{|S|} P[cover all q in S].  None if any needed
    joint-cover term exceeds cost_cap."""
    tot = 0.0
    for r in range(len(T) + 1):
        for S in combinations(T, r):
            jc = joint_cover_prob(allowed, list(S), cost_cap, memo)
            if jc is None:
                return None
            tot += ((-1) ** r) * jc
    return tot


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# cluster expansion
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
def ie_cost_log2(block):
    """log2 of the nested-I-E cost of a block = sum of all but the largest."""
    if len(block) <= 1:
        return 0
    return sum(block) - max(block)


def greedy_blocks(B, cost_cap):
    """Partition the active primes into consecutive blocks, each with I-E
    cost <= cost_cap, greedily packing the SMALLEST primes together (they
    carry the strongest correlations).  Coarser blocks => tighter FKG
    lower bound."""
    blocks, cur = [], []
    for q in B:
        if not cur:
            cur = [q]
            continue
        if (1 << ie_cost_log2(cur + [q])) <= cost_cap:
            cur.append(q)
        else:
            blocks.append(cur)
            cur = [q]
    if cur:
        blocks.append(cur)
    return blocks


def block_lower_bound(allowed, blocks, cost_cap, memo=None):
    """ln of the FKG block lower bound: A_k >= 2^N * prod_blocks P[miss
    within block].  Each block's joint-miss prob is exact (nested I-E).
    Returns (ln_lower, ok)."""
    N = len(allowed)
    tot = N * LN2
    for g in blocks:
        pm = P_miss(allowed, list(g), cost_cap, memo)
        if pm is None or pm <= 0.0:
            return None, False
        tot += math.log(pm)
    return tot, True


def best_single_block(B, cost_cap):
    """The largest prefix of B (smallest primes) whose single-block I-E is
    within the cap -- gives the tightest feasible UPPER bound
    2^N * P[miss within that block] >= A_k."""
    g = []
    for q in B:
        if (1 << ie_cost_log2(g + [q])) <= cost_cap:
            g.append(q)
        else:
            break
    return g


def cluster_term(T, lnP):
    """c_T = sum_{U subset T} (-1)^{|T|-|U|} ln P_U.  None if any ln P_U
    unavailable."""
    Tl = list(T)
    s = 0.0
    for r in range(len(Tl) + 1):
        for U in combinations(Tl, r):
            v = lnP.get(frozenset(U))
            if v is None:
                return None
            s += ((-1) ** (len(Tl) - r)) * v
    return s


def estimate(k, rmax=4, core_cut=None, cost_cap=1 << 20, max_states=6_000_000,
             want_exact=True):
    """Mean-field lower bound + cluster truncations r=1..rmax + rigorous
    count_tm upper bound + (if feasible) exact ln A_k.

    core_cut: only cluster over active primes <= core_cut (larger active
    primes stay at mean-field order; justified because p_q ~ 1 there)."""
    allowed = allowed_offsets(k)
    enf = enforceable_primes(k, allowed)
    B, W, dropped = reduce_primes(k, allowed, enf)
    N = len(allowed)
    base = N * LN2

    lnp, pq = {}, {}
    for q in B:
        lnp[q], pq[q] = marginal_lnp(allowed, q)
    mf_all = sum(lnp[q] for q in B)
    meanfield = base + mf_all                       # all-singletons FKG lower

    memo = {}                                       # shared joint-cover cache

    # rigorous FKG block lower bound (coarser partition => tighter)
    blocks = greedy_blocks(B, cost_cap)
    block_lower, _ = block_lower_bound(allowed, blocks, cost_cap, memo)

    # rigorous single-block upper bound: 2^N P[miss within G] >= A_k
    Gup = best_single_block(B, cost_cap)
    pm_up = P_miss(allowed, Gup, cost_cap, memo)
    upper_ie = base + math.log(pm_up) if (pm_up and pm_up > 0) else None

    core = list(B) if core_cut is None else [q for q in B if q <= core_cut]

    # ln P_T for every subset of core with 1 <= |T| <= rmax (singletons are
    # the exact marginals; |T|>=2 via nested I-E)
    lnP = {frozenset(): 0.0}
    for q in core:
        lnP[frozenset((q,))] = lnp[q]
    skipped = []
    for r in range(2, min(rmax, len(core)) + 1):
        for T in combinations(core, r):
            pm = P_miss(allowed, list(T), cost_cap, memo)
            if pm is None or pm <= 0.0:
                lnP[frozenset(T)] = None
                skipped.append(tuple(T))
            else:
                lnP[frozenset(T)] = math.log(pm)

    # cluster truncations
    trunc = {}
    cluster_contrib = {1: mf_all}
    for r in range(2, rmax + 1):
        if r > len(core):
            break
        s = 0.0
        for T in combinations(core, r):
            cT = cluster_term(T, lnP)
            if cT is not None:
                s += cT
        cluster_contrib[r] = s
    for rr in range(1, rmax + 1):
        tot = base
        for r in range(1, rr + 1):
            tot += cluster_contrib.get(r, 0.0)
        trunc[rr] = tot

    # exact ln A_k via the S519 transfer matrix on the full active set, but
    # ONLY when it is feasible (small k) -- prefixes are nested so we climb
    # and stop at the first abort (never pays the slow full-B abort).
    exact = None
    if want_exact and N <= 40:                 # k <= 80: full B count_tm fits
        last = None
        for i in range(1, len(B) + 1):
            c, st = count_tm(k, list(B[:i]), allowed, max_states=max_states,
                             want_stats=True)
            if c is None:
                last = None
                break
            last = (math.log(c), B[:i])
        if last is not None and last[1] == B:
            exact = last[0]

    return {
        "k": k, "N": N, "B": B, "W": W, "core": core, "base": base,
        "meanfield": meanfield, "block_lower": block_lower, "blocks": blocks,
        "upper": upper_ie, "upper_B": Gup, "trunc": trunc,
        "cluster_contrib": cluster_contrib, "exact": exact, "lnp": lnp,
        "pq": pq, "skipped": skipped,
    }


def ratio(lnval, k):
    return lnval / (k / math.log(k))


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# reporting
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
def report_one(k, rmax, core_cut, cost_cap, max_states, verbose=False):
    t0 = time.time()
    r = estimate(k, rmax, core_cut, cost_cap, max_states, want_exact=True)
    dt = time.time() - t0
    kk = k / math.log(k)
    print(f"\nk={k}  N={r['N']}  active B={r['B']} (W={r['W']})  "
          f"core={r['core']}  k/lnk={kk:.3f}  [{dt:.1f}s]")
    if verbose:
        print("   prime   class sizes        p_q        ln p_q")
        allowed = allowed_offsets(k)
        for q in r["B"]:
            sz = class_sizes(allowed, q)
            print(f"   {q:5d}   n in [{min(sz)},{max(sz)}]      "
                  f"{r['pq'][q]:.4e}  {r['lnp'][q]:9.4f}")
    ex = r["exact"]
    if ex is not None:
        print(f"  EXACT  ln A_k        = {ex:8.4f}   ratio = {ratio(ex,k):.4f}")
    print("  --- rigorous bracket (FKG block lower, single-block I-E upper) ---")
    print(f"  UPPER  block {r['upper_B']} = {r['upper']:8.4f}   "
          f"ratio = {ratio(r['upper'], k):.4f}")
    bl = r["block_lower"]
    if bl is not None:
        print(f"  LOWER  blocks {r['blocks']} = {bl:8.4f}   "
              f"ratio = {ratio(bl, k):.4f}")
    print(f"  (mean field, all-singleton FKG lower = {r['meanfield']:8.4f}   "
          f"ratio = {ratio(r['meanfield'], k):.4f})")
    print("  --- cluster-expansion point estimates (not one-sided) ---")
    for rr in sorted(r["trunc"]):
        if rr == 1:
            continue
        v = r["trunc"][rr]
        err = f"   err {v-ex:+.4f}" if ex is not None else ""
        print(f"  cluster r<={rr}         = {v:8.4f}   "
              f"ratio = {ratio(v, k):.4f}{err}")
    if r["skipped"]:
        print(f"  ({len(r['skipped'])} clusters skipped over cost cap "
              f"2^{int(math.log2(cost_cap))}: e.g. {r['skipped'][:4]})")
    return r


def _ls_slope(pts):
    n = len(pts)
    sx = sum(x for x, _ in pts)
    sy = sum(y for _, y in pts)
    sxx = sum(x * x for x, _ in pts)
    sxy = sum(x * y for x, y in pts)
    return (n * sxy - sx * sy) / (n * sxx - sx * sx)


def report_scan(kmin, kmax, rmax, core_cut, cost_cap, max_states):
    ks = [1 << m for m in range(2, 20) if kmin <= (1 << m) <= kmax]
    print(f"{'k':>6} {'N':>4} {'|B|':>3} {'exact':>9} {'LOWER':>9} "
          f"{'UPPER':>9} {'clus_r4':>9} | {'rt_ex':>7} {'rt_lo':>7} "
          f"{'rt_up':>7} {'rt_cl':>7}")
    recs = []
    for k in ks:
        r = estimate(k, rmax, core_cut, cost_cap, max_states, want_exact=True)
        recs.append(r)

        def fmt(v, w=9):
            return f"{v:{w}.3f}" if v is not None else f"{'--':>{w}}"

        def rt(v, w=7):
            return f"{ratio(v,k):{w}.4f}" if v is not None else f"{'--':>{w}}"
        ex, lo, up = r["exact"], r["block_lower"], r["upper"]
        cl = r["trunc"].get(min(rmax, 4)) or r["trunc"].get(rmax)
        print(f"{k:>6} {r['N']:>4} {len(r['B']):>3} {fmt(ex)} {fmt(lo)} "
              f"{fmt(up)} {fmt(cl)} | {rt(ex)} {rt(lo)} {rt(up)} {rt(cl)}")

    print("\nclean family k=2^m  (slope of ln(.) vs k/ln k -> conjecture 1.0):")
    for name, getter in (("exact", lambda r: r["exact"]),
                         ("FKG block UPPER", lambda r: r["upper"]),
                         ("FKG block LOWER", lambda r: r["block_lower"]),
                         ("mean field (singletons)",
                          lambda r: r["meanfield"])):
        pts = [(r["k"] / math.log(r["k"]), getter(r))
               for r in recs if getter(r) is not None]
        if len(pts) >= 2:
            sl = _ls_slope(pts)
            print(f"  {name:24s}: slope = {sl:.4f}   "
                  f"last ratio = {pts[-1][1] / pts[-1][0]:.4f}")

    print("\nRIGOROUS bracket on the entropy ratio ln A_k / (k/ln k):")
    for r in recs:
        lo, up = r["block_lower"], r["upper"]
        ex = r["exact"]
        tag = f"  (exact {ratio(ex,r['k']):.4f})" if ex is not None else \
              "  [exact unreachable -- bracket is the result]"
        if lo is not None and up is not None:
            print(f"  k={r['k']:>4}:  {ratio(lo,r['k']):.4f}  <=  "
                  f"ratio  <=  {ratio(up,r['k']):.4f}{tag}")


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# selftest
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
def selftest():
    print("=== census_entropy_asymptotic selftest ===")
    n_ok = 0

    # 1. marginal p_q (product) == count_tm({q})/2^N
    for k in (16, 32, 64):
        allowed = allowed_offsets(k)
        N = len(allowed)
        for q in enforceable_primes(k, allowed)[:4]:
            lp, p = marginal_lnp(allowed, q)
            lp_tm = math.log(count_tm(k, [q], allowed)) - N * LN2
            assert abs(lp - lp_tm) < 1e-9, (k, q, lp, lp_tm)
    n_ok += 1
    print("[1] marginal p_q (class-size product) == count_tm({q})/2^N")

    # 2. joint cover I-E == count_tm joint miss, bit-for-bit, pairs+triples
    for k in (32, 64):
        allowed = allowed_offsets(k)
        N = len(allowed)
        B, _, _ = reduce_primes(k, allowed)
        tests = [B[:2], B[:3]]
        if len(B) >= 5:
            tests += [list(B[2:5]), list(B[1:4])]
        for T in tests:
            ie = P_miss(allowed, list(T))
            tm = count_tm(k, list(T), allowed) / (2.0 ** N)
            assert abs(ie - tm) <= 1e-12 + 1e-9 * abs(tm), (k, T, ie, tm)
    n_ok += 1
    print("[2] joint-cover nested I-E == count_tm (pairs+triples, k=32,64)")

    # 3. Mobius identity: full cluster sum (r=|B|) == ln A_k - N ln2.
    #    P_T from count_tm (feasible for any subset at k<=64; the full-B
    #    nested-I-E would be 2^{sum of all but max} -- too slow -- which is
    #    exactly why we TRUNCATE; the IE engine itself is checked in [2]).
    for k in (8, 16, 32, 64):
        allowed = allowed_offsets(k)
        B, _, _ = reduce_primes(k, allowed)
        N = len(allowed)
        lnP = {frozenset(): 0.0}
        for r in range(1, len(B) + 1):
            for T in combinations(B, r):
                lnP[frozenset(T)] = math.log(count_tm(k, list(T), allowed)) \
                    - N * LN2
        total = 0.0
        for r in range(1, len(B) + 1):
            for T in combinations(B, r):
                total += cluster_term(T, lnP)
        lnA = math.log(count_tm(k, list(B), allowed))
        assert abs((N * LN2 + total) - lnA) < 1e-7, (k, N * LN2 + total, lnA)
    n_ok += 1
    print("[3] full cluster sum (r=|B|) == ln A_k - N ln2 (Mobius exact)")

    # 4. mean field <= exact A_k (FKG lower bound), k=8..64
    for k in (8, 16, 32, 48, 64):
        r = estimate(k, rmax=1, want_exact=True)
        assert r["exact"] is not None
        assert r["meanfield"] <= r["exact"] + 1e-9, \
            (k, r["meanfield"], r["exact"])
    n_ok += 1
    print("[4] mean field <= exact ln A_k (FKG lower bound), k=8..64")

    # 5. rigorous upper bound: count_tm(prefix) >= A_k, monotone
    for k in (16, 32, 64):
        allowed = allowed_offsets(k)
        B, _, _ = reduce_primes(k, allowed)
        A = count_tm(k, list(B), allowed)
        prev = None
        for i in range(1, len(B) + 1):
            up = count_tm(k, list(B[:i]), allowed)
            assert up >= A, (k, B[:i], up, A)
            if prev is not None:
                assert up <= prev, (k, i, up, prev)   # monotone non-increasing
            prev = up
    n_ok += 1
    print("[5] count_tm(prefix of B) >= A_k, monotone (rigorous upper bound)")

    # 6. cluster error shrinks with r at validated k; r<=3 within 1% at k=64.
    #    (rmax=3: every cluster of order <=3 is below the default cost cap at
    #    k<=64, so the truncations are complete -- no skips.)
    for k, rm in ((32, 3), (64, 3)):
        r = estimate(k, rmax=rm, want_exact=True)
        ex = r["exact"]
        errs = [abs(r["trunc"][rr] - ex) for rr in sorted(r["trunc"])]
        for a, b in zip(errs, errs[1:]):
            assert b <= a + 1e-9, (k, errs)
    r64 = estimate(64, rmax=3, want_exact=True)
    assert abs(r64["trunc"][3] - r64["exact"]) / abs(r64["exact"]) < 0.01, \
        (r64["trunc"][3], r64["exact"])
    n_ok += 1
    print("[6] cluster error shrinks with r; r<=3 within 1% at k=64")

    # 7. alternating sign of the truncation error (odd r under, even over)
    #    at validated k=32,64 for r=1,2,3 -- the empirical-bracket basis
    for k in (32, 64):
        r = estimate(k, rmax=3, want_exact=True)
        ex = r["exact"]
        for rr in (1, 2, 3):
            if rr >= len(r["B"]):
                continue                       # exact at/after full order
            e = r["trunc"][rr] - ex
            if rr % 2 == 1:
                assert e <= 1e-9, (k, rr, e)   # odd: under
            else:
                assert e >= -1e-9, (k, rr, e)  # even: over
    n_ok += 1
    print("[7] truncation error alternates: odd r under, even r over (k=32,64)")

    # 8. exact field == known A_k / DFS
    for k in (8, 16, 32, 64):
        allowed = allowed_offsets(k)
        B, _, _ = reduce_primes(k, allowed)
        assert count_tm(k, list(B), allowed) == KNOWN[k], k
    assert abs(math.exp(estimate(16, rmax=2)["exact"])
               - count_admissible_dfs(16)) < 0.5
    n_ok += 1
    print("[8] count_tm(B) == known A_k {8,16,32,64}; exact == DFS at k=16")

    # 9. cost cap behaves: a cluster over the cap is skipped (None), and an
    #    estimate at a lower cap is still produced (graceful degradation)
    allowed = allowed_offsets(128)
    assert joint_cover_prob(allowed, [11, 13, 17], cost_cap=1 << 18) is None
    assert joint_cover_prob(allowed, [3, 5, 7], cost_cap=1 << 18) is not None
    rr = estimate(128, rmax=3, cost_cap=1 << 16, want_exact=False)
    assert rr["meanfield"] < rr["trunc"][2]            # mean field below r=2
    assert rr["trunc"].get(2) is not None
    n_ok += 1
    print("[9] cost cap skips over-budget clusters; estimate still produced")

    # 10. the rigorous bracket BRACKETS exact, and the block lower bound is a
    #     genuine improvement over the all-singletons mean field, k=8..64
    for k in (16, 32, 48, 64):
        r = estimate(k, rmax=3, want_exact=True)
        ex = r["exact"]
        assert ex is not None
        assert r["block_lower"] <= ex + 1e-9, (k, "block_lower>exact",
                                               r["block_lower"], ex)
        assert r["upper"] >= ex - 1e-9, (k, "upper<exact", r["upper"], ex)
        assert r["meanfield"] <= r["block_lower"] + 1e-9, \
            (k, "mf>block_lower")
    n_ok += 1
    print("[10] FKG bracket: block_lower <= exact <= upper; "
          "mean field <= block_lower (k=16..64)")

    # 11. coarsening the partition monotonically tightens the FKG lower bound:
    #     a single block {3,5,7} >= product of {3,5}*{7} >= product of
    #     {3}*{5}*{7} (all <= exact), at k=64
    allowed = allowed_offsets(64)
    N = len(allowed)
    one = N * LN2 + math.log(P_miss(allowed, [3, 5, 7]))
    two = N * LN2 + math.log(P_miss(allowed, [3, 5])) + \
        math.log(P_miss(allowed, [7]))
    three = N * LN2 + sum(marginal_lnp(allowed, q)[0] for q in (3, 5, 7))
    ex357 = math.log(count_tm(64, [3, 5, 7], allowed))
    assert three <= two + 1e-9 <= one + 1e-9 <= ex357 + 1e-9, \
        (three, two, one, ex357)
    n_ok += 1
    print("[11] coarser FKG partition tightens the lower bound monotonically")

    print(f"\nALL SELFTESTS PASSED ({n_ok} groups)")


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--selftest", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--k", type=int, default=0)
    ap.add_argument("--scan", type=int, nargs=2, default=None,
                    metavar=("KMIN", "KMAX"))
    ap.add_argument("--rmax", type=int, default=4)
    ap.add_argument("--core-cut", type=int, default=None)
    ap.add_argument("--cost-cap", type=int, default=20,
                    help="log2 of the joint-cover I-E cost cap (default 20)")
    ap.add_argument("--max-states", type=int, default=6_000_000)
    ap.add_argument("--verbose", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    cap = 1 << args.cost_cap
    if args.selftest:
        selftest()
    elif args.k:
        report_one(args.k, args.rmax, args.core_cut, cap, args.max_states,
                   args.verbose)
    elif args.scan:
        report_scan(args.scan[0], args.scan[1], args.rmax, args.core_cut,
                    cap, args.max_states)
    else:
        selftest()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

1	# The census entropy constant via a cluster expansion: a validated estimator and a tight rigorous bracket (S520)
2	
3	## Question (open item 4, PROGRAM.md NEXT ACTION after S519)
4	
5	S519 closed the transfer-matrix route to the *exact* `A_k` (state space
6	Θ(A_k)) and reduced the count to the active primes `B(k) ~ ρ*(k) ~
7	k/ln k`:
8	
9	> `A_k = #{ S ⊆ allowed(k) : for every prime q ∈ B(k), the occupied
10	> residues {o mod q : o ∈ S} do NOT cover all of Z_q }`.
11	
12	The remaining question is purely asymptotic — the conjecture
13	`A_k = e^{(1+o(1))·π(k)}`, i.e. `ln A_k / (k/ln k) → 1`. The S519 NEXT
14	ACTION asked for an estimate of that constant **without** exact counting,
15	via a generating-function / cluster-expansion analysis, validated against
16	the exact `A_k` (k ≤ 64) before extrapolating.
17	
18	**Result.** Built `census_entropy_asymptotic.py`, an exact
19	reformulation + cluster expansion that (i) reproduces the exact `A_k`
20	ratio at k ≤ 64, (ii) gives a **rigorous two-sided bracket** on the
21	entropy ratio that scales past the exact-counting wall, and (iii) shows
22	the constant's approach to 1 is **driven by the CRT correlations, not the
23	independent-prime leading term**. Headline:
24	
25	```
26	   k     ln A_k / (k/ln k)              method
27	   8        0.6667   (exact)
28	  16        0.8081   (exact)
29	  32        0.8861   (exact)
30	  64        0.9276   (exact)              bracket [0.9236, 0.9276] contains it
31	 128     ∈ [0.9243, 0.9403]  RIGOROUS     cluster point estimate 0.9264
32	 256     ≥ 0.9282            RIGOROUS lo  (upper bound loose, see below)
33	```
34	
35	The ratio climbs monotonically `0.667 → 0.808 → 0.886 → 0.928 → ≈0.93`,
36	consistent with `→ 1`, but the convergence is slow and the constant `= 1`
37	is **not** proved — what blocks it is now measured precisely (below).
38	
39	## The exact reformulation (this is the key)
40	
41	Put the uniform measure on subsets: each allowed offset is included
42	independently with probability ½. Then
43	
44	> `A_k = 2^N · P[ admissible ]`,  `N = |allowed(k)| = φ(k)`,  **exactly**
45	
46	(every subset has probability `2^{-N}`). Let `C_q` = "S covers every
47	class mod q" (an *increasing* event) and `\bar C_q` = "S misses a class
48	mod q" (*decreasing*). `admissible = ∩_{q∈B(k)} \bar C_q`.
49	
50	- **Marginal** (offsets in distinct classes mod q are disjoint):
51	  `p_q = P[\bar C_q] = 1 − ∏_j (1 − 2^{−n_{q,j}})`, exact from the class
52	  sizes `n_{q,j}` — no transfer matrix.
53	- **Mean field** = the independent-primes product `∏_q p_q`. Since the
54	  `\bar C_q` are decreasing, they are positively associated (FKG), so
55	  `P[∩] ≥ ∏_q p_q` ⇒ `A_k ≥ 2^N ∏_q p_q` is a **rigorous lower bound**.
56	- **Cluster expansion** (the corrections = CRT overlaps). For `T ⊆ B(k)`
57	  let `P_T = P[∩_{q∈T} \bar C_q]`. Möbius inversion of `f(T)=ln P_T`
58	  gives the connected cluster terms
59	  `c_T = Σ_{U⊆T} (−1)^{|T|−|U|} ln P_U`, with
60	  `ln P_B = Σ_{∅≠T⊆B} c_T` **exactly**. Truncating at `|T| ≤ r` is the
61	  order-r approximation; `r=1` is the mean field.
62	
63	## The engine: joint cover by nested inclusion–exclusion
64	
65	`P_T` needs the joint cover probabilities `P[∩_{q∈S} C_q]`. These have a
66	nested-I-E form with the largest prime `L ∈ S` as the product prime:
67	
68	```
69	P[cover all q∈S] = Σ_{(U_h ⊆ Z_h)_h}  (−1)^{Σ|U_h|}
70	                   · 2^{−(#offsets in any head-class U_h)}
71	                   · ∏_{w∈Z_L} (1 − 2^{−n_w}),
72	        n_w = #offsets with (mod L = w) and (mod h ∉ U_h for every head h).
73	```
74	
75	Cost `= 2^{(sum of S) − max(S)}` — tiny for the small primes that
76	dominate the entropy and **independent of k**. Validated **bit-for-bit**
77	against the S519 transfer matrix `count_tm` (selftest [2], pairs+triples
78	over k=32,64; reldiff 0). This is why the method survives past k=64:
79	`count_tm` on the full `B(k)` has Θ(A_k) states, but a 3–5-prime cluster
80	or block needs only a `2^{O(small primes)}` I-E.
81	
82	## Validation against exact `A_k` (k ≤ 64)
83	
84	The cluster truncations at k=64 (B = {3,5,7,11,13}, exact ln A = 14.2741;
85	`--k 64 --rmax 5 --cost-cap 27`):
86	
87	```
88	   r=1 (mean field) 11.5697  ratio 0.7518  err −2.7044
89	   r=2              14.8597  ratio 0.9656  err +0.5855
90	   r=3              14.1629  ratio 0.9203  err −0.1113
91	   r=4              14.2865  ratio 0.9284  err +0.0124
92	   r=5 (= full B)   14.2741  ratio 0.9276  err  0       (= exact, Möbius)
93	```
94	
95	The errors **alternate in sign (odd r under, even r over) and shrink
96	≈5–9× per order** (|err| ratios 0.22, 0.19, 0.11) — a convergent
97	expansion; r=4 matches exact to 0.012 (0.08% of ln A). Selftests [3]
98	(Möbius identity = exact at full order), [4] (mean field ≤ exact, FKG),
99	[6]/[7] (error shrinks + alternates) assert this. At k=32 the bracket is
100	exact (B has 3 primes); at k=16, 2 primes.
101	
102	## The rigorous bracket (FKG blocks) — what scales
103	
104	The mean field is a weak lower bound at large k (the correlations are
105	huge — see below). A much tighter **rigorous** bracket comes from FKG
106	applied to *blocks*:
107	
108	- **Lower bound** — for any partition of `B(k)` into blocks,
109	  `P[∩_{B}] ≥ ∏_{blocks g} P[∩_{q∈g} \bar C_q]` (FKG, decreasing events),
110	  each block's joint-miss exact by the I-E engine. Coarser blocks ⇒
111	  tighter (selftest [11], monotone); we greedily pack the smallest
112	  (most-correlated) primes into the largest block the cost cap allows.
113	- **Upper bound** — `A_k ≤ 2^N P[∩_{q∈G} \bar C_q]` for any single block
114	  `G ⊆ B` (dropping the other constraints), exact by I-E. Larger `G` ⇒
115	  tighter.
116	
117	Both bracket the exact value (selftest [10]). Measured:
118	
119	```
120	   k     LOWER (ratio)     UPPER (ratio)    block G / partition          exact
121	  64    14.212 (0.9236)   14.274 (0.9276)   up G={3,5,7,11}; lo +{13}    0.9276 ✓in
122	 128    24.385 (0.9243)   24.806 (0.9403)   G={3,5,7,11,13} (cost 2^26)    —
123	 256    42.851 (0.9282)   51.986 (1.1261)   up G={3,5,7,11}; lo +pairs     —
124	```
125	
126	(k=64/256 at cost cap 2^20; k=128 at 2^26. At cap 2^27 the k=64 single
127	block IS the full B={3,5,7,11,13}, so there the bracket collapses to the
128	exact 0.9276. `--k 128 --cost-cap 27 --rmax 1` reproduces the k=128 row;
129	the upper {3,5,7,11,13} = 24.806 leaves only {17,19,23} unconstrained.)
130	
131	- **k=128: ratio ∈ [0.9243, 0.9403]** — a rigorous pin to ≈0.932 ± 0.008,
132	  with the cluster point estimate 0.9264 inside it. (At a smaller cost
133	  cap 2^20 the bound is the looser [0.889, 0.941]; the 2^26 block
134	  {3,5,7,11,13} tightens the lower bound by recapturing the 13-correlation
135	  — reproduce with `--k 128 --cost-cap 27 --rmax 1`.)
136	- **k=256: ratio ≥ 0.9282** (rigorous). The *upper* bound is loose
137	  (1.126) because a single feasible block holds only 4 of the **14**
138	  active primes — constraining 4 of 14 leaves far too many subsets. This
139	  is the honest limitation: the rigorous upper bound degrades as `|B(k)|`
140	  grows, so the bracket closes to a point only at small k (it is exact at
141	  k≤64, tight at k=128, one-sided-useful at k=256).
142	
143	## The structural finding: the constant is a CORRELATION effect
144	
145	The independent-prime (mean-field) ratio **falls** with k:
146	
147	```
148	   k      mean-field ratio     true ratio (exact / bracket)
149	  64         0.752                0.928
150	 128         0.605                ≈0.93
151	 256         0.394                ≥0.928 (lower bound)
152	```
153	
154	So the naive "leading term `∏_q P[miss mod q]`" does **not** approach 1 —
155	it declines. The CRT correlations supply a *growing* fraction of the
156	entropy (≈19% at k=64, ≈35% at k=128, ≈57% at k=256 of `ln A_k` comes
157	from beyond the independent product). The conjecture's `→1` is therefore
158	**carried by the correlations**, not the leading term. This is why the
159	exponent is exactly `π(k)` (= the W(B)=ρ*(k) admissible-geometry of S519)
160	and not something the independent product alone predicts.
161	
162	## What this delivers / what stays open
163	
164	- **Delivered:** a working, validated estimator for the entropy constant
165	  (exact reformulation, FKG mean-field lower bound, cluster expansion with
166	  the nested-I-E engine, FKG block bracket). Exact at k≤64; a **rigorous
167	  bracket `[0.9243, 0.9403]` at k=128** (the next clean target after
168	  k=64); rigorous lower bound `0.928` at k=256. The monotone climb
169	  `0.667 → 0.808 → 0.886 → 0.928 → ≈0.93` is consistent with `→1`.
170	- **The key structural fact:** the entropy is correlation-dominated; the
171	  independent-prime term gives a constant that *declines* (0.75→0.61→0.39),

# The census entropy constant via a cluster expansion: a validated estimator and a tight rigorous bracket (S520)

## Question (open item 4, PROGRAM.md NEXT ACTION after S519)

S519 closed the transfer-matrix route to the *exact* `A_k` (state space
Θ(A_k)) and reduced the count to the active primes `B(k) ~ ρ*(k) ~
k/ln k`:

> `A_k = #{ S ⊆ allowed(k) : for every prime q ∈ B(k), the occupied
> residues {o mod q : o ∈ S} do NOT cover all of Z_q }`.

The remaining question is purely asymptotic — the conjecture
`A_k = e^{(1+o(1))·π(k)}`, i.e. `ln A_k / (k/ln k) → 1`. The S519 NEXT
ACTION asked for an estimate of that constant **without** exact counting,
via a generating-function / cluster-expansion analysis, validated against
the exact `A_k` (k ≤ 64) before extrapolating.

**Result.** Built `census_entropy_asymptotic.py`, an exact
reformulation + cluster expansion that (i) reproduces the exact `A_k`
ratio at k ≤ 64, (ii) gives a **rigorous two-sided bracket** on the
entropy ratio that scales past the exact-counting wall, and (iii) shows
the constant's approach to 1 is **driven by the CRT correlations, not the
independent-prime leading term**. Headline:

```
   k     ln A_k / (k/ln k)              method
   8        0.6667   (exact)
  16        0.8081   (exact)
  32        0.8861   (exact)
  64        0.9276   (exact)              bracket [0.9236, 0.9276] contains it
 128     ∈ [0.9243, 0.9403]  RIGOROUS     cluster point estimate 0.9264
 256     ≥ 0.9282            RIGOROUS lo  (upper bound loose, see below)
```

The ratio climbs monotonically `0.667 → 0.808 → 0.886 → 0.928 → ≈0.93`,
consistent with `→ 1`, but the convergence is slow and the constant `= 1`
is **not** proved — what blocks it is now measured precisely (below).

## The exact reformulation (this is the key)

Put the uniform measure on subsets: each allowed offset is included
independently with probability ½. Then

> `A_k = 2^N · P[ admissible ]`,  `N = |allowed(k)| = φ(k)`,  **exactly**

(every subset has probability `2^{-N}`). Let `C_q` = "S covers every
class mod q" (an *increasing* event) and `\bar C_q` = "S misses a class
mod q" (*decreasing*). `admissible = ∩_{q∈B(k)} \bar C_q`.

- **Marginal** (offsets in distinct classes mod q are disjoint):
  `p_q = P[\bar C_q] = 1 − ∏_j (1 − 2^{−n_{q,j}})`, exact from the class
  sizes `n_{q,j}` — no transfer matrix.
- **Mean field** = the independent-primes product `∏_q p_q`. Since the
  `\bar C_q` are decreasing, they are positively associated (FKG), so
  `P[∩] ≥ ∏_q p_q` ⇒ `A_k ≥ 2^N ∏_q p_q` is a **rigorous lower bound**.
- **Cluster expansion** (the corrections = CRT overlaps). For `T ⊆ B(k)`
  let `P_T = P[∩_{q∈T} \bar C_q]`. Möbius inversion of `f(T)=ln P_T`
  gives the connected cluster terms
  `c_T = Σ_{U⊆T} (−1)^{|T|−|U|} ln P_U`, with
  `ln P_B = Σ_{∅≠T⊆B} c_T` **exactly**. Truncating at `|T| ≤ r` is the
  order-r approximation; `r=1` is the mean field.

## The engine: joint cover by nested inclusion–exclusion

`P_T` needs the joint cover probabilities `P[∩_{q∈S} C_q]`. These have a
nested-I-E form with the largest prime `L ∈ S` as the product prime:

```
P[cover all q∈S] = Σ_{(U_h ⊆ Z_h)_h}  (−1)^{Σ|U_h|}
                   · 2^{−(#offsets in any head-class U_h)}
                   · ∏_{w∈Z_L} (1 − 2^{−n_w}),
        n_w = #offsets with (mod L = w) and (mod h ∉ U_h for every head h).
```

Cost `= 2^{(sum of S) − max(S)}` — tiny for the small primes that
dominate the entropy and **independent of k**. Validated **bit-for-bit**
against the S519 transfer matrix `count_tm` (selftest [2], pairs+triples
over k=32,64; reldiff 0). This is why the method survives past k=64:
`count_tm` on the full `B(k)` has Θ(A_k) states, but a 3–5-prime cluster
or block needs only a `2^{O(small primes)}` I-E.

## Validation against exact `A_k` (k ≤ 64)

The cluster truncations at k=64 (B = {3,5,7,11,13}, exact ln A = 14.2741;
`--k 64 --rmax 5 --cost-cap 27`):

```
   r=1 (mean field) 11.5697  ratio 0.7518  err −2.7044
   r=2              14.8597  ratio 0.9656  err +0.5855
   r=3              14.1629  ratio 0.9203  err −0.1113
   r=4              14.2865  ratio 0.9284  err +0.0124
   r=5 (= full B)   14.2741  ratio 0.9276  err  0       (= exact, Möbius)
```

The errors **alternate in sign (odd r under, even r over) and shrink
≈5–9× per order** (|err| ratios 0.22, 0.19, 0.11) — a convergent
expansion; r=4 matches exact to 0.012 (0.08% of ln A). Selftests [3]
(Möbius identity = exact at full order), [4] (mean field ≤ exact, FKG),
[6]/[7] (error shrinks + alternates) assert this. At k=32 the bracket is
exact (B has 3 primes); at k=16, 2 primes.

## The rigorous bracket (FKG blocks) — what scales

The mean field is a weak lower bound at large k (the correlations are
huge — see below). A much tighter **rigorous** bracket comes from FKG
applied to *blocks*:

- **Lower bound** — for any partition of `B(k)` into blocks,
  `P[∩_{B}] ≥ ∏_{blocks g} P[∩_{q∈g} \bar C_q]` (FKG, decreasing events),
  each block's joint-miss exact by the I-E engine. Coarser blocks ⇒
  tighter (selftest [11], monotone); we greedily pack the smallest
  (most-correlated) primes into the largest block the cost cap allows.
- **Upper bound** — `A_k ≤ 2^N P[∩_{q∈G} \bar C_q]` for any single block
  `G ⊆ B` (dropping the other constraints), exact by I-E. Larger `G` ⇒
  tighter.

Both bracket the exact value (selftest [10]). Measured:

```
   k     LOWER (ratio)     UPPER (ratio)    block G / partition          exact
  64    14.212 (0.9236)   14.274 (0.9276)   up G={3,5,7,11}; lo +{13}    0.9276 ✓in
 128    24.385 (0.9243)   24.806 (0.9403)   G={3,5,7,11,13} (cost 2^26)    —
 256    42.851 (0.9282)   51.986 (1.1261)   up G={3,5,7,11}; lo +pairs     —
```

(k=64/256 at cost cap 2^20; k=128 at 2^26. At cap 2^27 the k=64 single
block IS the full B={3,5,7,11,13}, so there the bracket collapses to the
exact 0.9276. `--k 128 --cost-cap 27 --rmax 1` reproduces the k=128 row;
the upper {3,5,7,11,13} = 24.806 leaves only {17,19,23} unconstrained.)

- **k=128: ratio ∈ [0.9243, 0.9403]** — a rigorous pin to ≈0.932 ± 0.008,
  with the cluster point estimate 0.9264 inside it. (At a smaller cost
  cap 2^20 the bound is the looser [0.889, 0.941]; the 2^26 block
  {3,5,7,11,13} tightens the lower bound by recapturing the 13-correlation
  — reproduce with `--k 128 --cost-cap 27 --rmax 1`.)
- **k=256: ratio ≥ 0.9282** (rigorous). The *upper* bound is loose
  (1.126) because a single feasible block holds only 4 of the **14**
  active primes — constraining 4 of 14 leaves far too many subsets. This
  is the honest limitation: the rigorous upper bound degrades as `|B(k)|`
  grows, so the bracket closes to a point only at small k (it is exact at
  k≤64, tight at k=128, one-sided-useful at k=256).

## The structural finding: the constant is a CORRELATION effect

The independent-prime (mean-field) ratio **falls** with k:

```
   k      mean-field ratio     true ratio (exact / bracket)
  64         0.752                0.928
 128         0.605                ≈0.93
 256         0.394                ≥0.928 (lower bound)
```

So the naive "leading term `∏_q P[miss mod q]`" does **not** approach 1 —
it declines. The CRT correlations supply a *growing* fraction of the
entropy (≈19% at k=64, ≈35% at k=128, ≈57% at k=256 of `ln A_k` comes
from beyond the independent product). The conjecture's `→1` is therefore
**carried by the correlations**, not the leading term. This is why the
exponent is exactly `π(k)` (= the W(B)=ρ*(k) admissible-geometry of S519)
and not something the independent product alone predicts.

## What this delivers / what stays open

- **Delivered:** a working, validated estimator for the entropy constant
  (exact reformulation, FKG mean-field lower bound, cluster expansion with
  the nested-I-E engine, FKG block bracket). Exact at k≤64; a **rigorous
  bracket `[0.9243, 0.9403]` at k=128** (the next clean target after
  k=64); rigorous lower bound `0.928` at k=256. The monotone climb
  `0.667 → 0.808 → 0.886 → 0.928 → ≈0.93` is consistent with `→1`.
- **The key structural fact:** the entropy is correlation-dominated; the
  independent-prime term gives a constant that *declines* (0.75→0.61→0.39),
  so the approach to 1 is entirely in the CRT-overlap corrections.
- **Still open (the constant = 1):** not proved. The bracket does not
  close to a point as `|B(k)| → ∞` at fixed cost — the rigorous upper
  bound degrades because a single feasible block covers a shrinking
  fraction of the active primes, and the cluster series, while convergent,
  has terms of size Θ(entropy) (the cap-sensitivity at k=128 shows the
  triple sum still moving as more clusters are admitted). Proving `=1`
  needs an analytic handle on the *full* correlation series (or the
  cross-block correlations) as k→∞ — the residual analytic piece S519
  flagged, now sharpened: it is not a small correction to control but the
  Θ(entropy)-sized correlation structure itself.

## What would falsify these results

- The rigorous bracket failing to contain the exact `A_k` at any
  validated k (FKG bug) — selftest [10] asserts `lower ≤ exact ≤ upper`
  for k=16..64; not observed.
- The joint-cover I-E disagreeing with `count_tm` — selftest [2], bit-for-
  bit on pairs+triples; reldiff 0.
- The full cluster sum (r=|B|) ≠ `ln A_k − N ln2` (Möbius bug) —
  selftest [3]; asserted to 1e-7.
- The mean field exceeding exact (lower-bound bug) — selftest [4]; the
  measured mean field is far *below* exact and declining.
- The cluster truncation error not shrinking / not alternating at
  validated k — selftest [6],[7]; if it failed, the expansion would not
  converge and the k=128 estimate would be void (it does converge).
- The block lower bound *not* monotone under coarsening (FKG bug) —
  selftest [11].

## Files

`census_entropy_asymptotic.py` (one script, `--selftest` (11 groups),
`--k`, `--scan KMIN KMAX`, `--rmax`, `--cost-cap`), this file. Reuses the
S519 `census_transfer_matrix.py` (`allowed_offsets`, `reduce_primes`,
`count_tm`) for the active-prime reduction and the validation oracle.
Cross-refs: `census_transfer_matrix_results.md` (the W(B)=ρ*(k)=π(k)
geometry that fixes the *exponent*; this file addresses the *constant*),
`local_pattern_census_results.md` (the A_k data and the entropy law).
```

LN2 = math.log(2.0)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# class sizes and the marginal p_q (exact, no transfer matrix)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
def class_sizes(allowed, q):
    per = [0] * q
    for o in allowed:
        per[o % q] += 1
    return per


def marginal_lnp(allowed, q):
    """ln p_q = ln P[S misses a class mod q], p=1/2.
    p_q = 1 - prod_j (1 - 2^{-n_j}); computed via log1p/expm1 so we never
    subtract two near-equal floats for tiny p_q."""
    ln_cover = 0.0
    for n in class_sizes(allowed, q):
        ln_cover += math.log1p(-(2.0 ** (-n)))
    pq = -math.expm1(ln_cover)
    if pq <= 0.0:                              # cover==1 to float precision
        pq = sum(2.0 ** (-n) for n in class_sizes(allowed, q))
    return math.log(pq), pq


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# joint cover probability via nested inclusion-exclusion (the engine)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
def joint_cover_prob(allowed, S, cost_cap=None, memo=None):
    """P[ intersection_{q in S} C_q ] = P[cover every class mod q, all q
    in S] under the uniform (p=1/2) measure.

    Nested I-E with the LARGEST prime as the product prime.  Cost =
    prod over head primes of 2^h = 2^{sum(S)-max(S)}.  Returns None if
    that exceeds cost_cap (caller treats the cluster as unavailable).
    S = [] -> 1.0 (empty cover).  `memo` (keyed by sorted-tuple) avoids
    recomputing the same joint cover (the costly large blocks recur in
    both the upper bound and the lower-bound partition)."""
    S = sorted(S)
    key = tuple(S)
    if memo is not None and key in memo:
        return memo[key]
    if not S:
        return 1.0
    heads, L = S[:-1], S[-1]
    leaves = 1
    for h in heads:
        leaves <<= h                            # 2^h
    if cost_cap is not None and leaves > cost_cap:
        if memo is not None:
            memo[key] = None
        return None
    no = len(allowed)
    # per-head per-residue offset bitmasks; per-L-class offset bitmasks
    head_cls = [[0] * h for h in heads]
    for i, o in enumerate(allowed):
        for hi, h in enumerate(heads):
            head_cls[hi][o % h] |= (1 << i)
    Lcls = [0] * L
    for i, o in enumerate(allowed):
        Lcls[o % L] |= (1 << i)

    total = 0.0
    # recurse over head subsets, accumulating the excluded-offset bitmask
    def rec(hi, excl_mask, sign):
        nonlocal total
        if hi == len(heads):
            excl = excl_mask.bit_count()
            prod = 2.0 ** (-excl)
            for w in range(L):
                n_w = (Lcls[w] & ~excl_mask).bit_count()
                prod *= (1.0 - 2.0 ** (-n_w))
            total += sign * prod
            return
        cls = head_cls[hi]
        h = heads[hi]
        for U in range(1 << h):
            m = 0
            uu = U
            r = 0
            while uu:
                if uu & 1:
                    m |= cls[r]
                uu >>= 1
                r += 1
            s = -sign if (U.bit_count() & 1) else sign
            rec(hi + 1, excl_mask | m, s)
    rec(0, 0, 1)
    if memo is not None:
        memo[key] = total
    return total


def P_miss(allowed, T, cost_cap=None, memo=None):
    """P[ intersection_{q in T} \bar C_q ] (miss a class mod every q in T)
    = sum_{S subset T} (-1)^{|S|} P[cover all q in S].  None if any needed
    joint-cover term exceeds cost_cap."""
    tot = 0.0
    for r in range(len(T) + 1):
        for S in combinations(T, r):
            jc = joint_cover_prob(allowed, list(S), cost_cap, memo)
            if jc is None:
                return None
            tot += ((-1) ** r) * jc
    return tot


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# cluster expansion
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
def ie_cost_log2(block):
    """log2 of the nested-I-E cost of a block = sum of all but the largest."""
    if len(block) <= 1:
        return 0
    return sum(block) - max(block)


def greedy_blocks(B, cost_cap):
    """Partition the active primes into consecutive blocks, each with I-E
    cost <= cost_cap, greedily packing the SMALLEST primes together (they
    carry the strongest correlations).  Coarser blocks => tighter FKG
    lower bound."""
    blocks, cur = [], []
    for q in B:
        if not cur:
            cur = [q]
            continue
        if (1 << ie_cost_log2(cur + [q])) <= cost_cap:
            cur.append(q)
        else:
            blocks.append(cur)
            cur = [q]
    if cur:
        blocks.append(cur)
    return blocks


def block_lower_bound(allowed, blocks, cost_cap, memo=None):
    """ln of the FKG block lower bound: A_k >= 2^N * prod_blocks P[miss
    within block].  Each block's joint-miss prob is exact (nested I-E).
    Returns (ln_lower, ok)."""
    N = len(allowed)
    tot = N * LN2
    for g in blocks:
        pm = P_miss(allowed, list(g), cost_cap, memo)
        if pm is None or pm <= 0.0:
            return None, False
        tot += math.log(pm)
    return tot, True


def best_single_block(B, cost_cap):
    """The largest prefix of B (smallest primes) whose single-block I-E is
    within the cap -- gives the tightest feasible UPPER bound
    2^N * P[miss within that block] >= A_k."""
    g = []
    for q in B:
        if (1 << ie_cost_log2(g + [q])) <= cost_cap:
            g.append(q)
        else:
            break
    return g


def cluster_term(T, lnP):
    """c_T = sum_{U subset T} (-1)^{|T|-|U|} ln P_U.  None if any ln P_U
    unavailable."""
    Tl = list(T)
    s = 0.0
    for r in range(len(Tl) + 1):
        for U in combinations(Tl, r):
            v = lnP.get(frozenset(U))
            if v is None:
                return None
            s += ((-1) ** (len(Tl) - r)) * v
    return s


def estimate(k, rmax=4, core_cut=None, cost_cap=1 << 20, max_states=6_000_000,
             want_exact=True):
    """Mean-field lower bound + cluster truncations r=1..rmax + rigorous
    count_tm upper bound + (if feasible) exact ln A_k.

    core_cut: only cluster over active primes <= core_cut (larger active
    primes stay at mean-field order; justified because p_q ~ 1 there)."""
    allowed = allowed_offsets(k)
    enf = enforceable_primes(k, allowed)
    B, W, dropped = reduce_primes(k, allowed, enf)
    N = len(allowed)
    base = N * LN2

    lnp, pq = {}, {}
    for q in B:
        lnp[q], pq[q] = marginal_lnp(allowed, q)
    mf_all = sum(lnp[q] for q in B)
    meanfield = base + mf_all                       # all-singletons FKG lower

    memo = {}                                       # shared joint-cover cache

    # rigorous FKG block lower bound (coarser partition => tighter)
    blocks = greedy_blocks(B, cost_cap)
    block_lower, _ = block_lower_bound(allowed, blocks, cost_cap, memo)

    # rigorous single-block upper bound: 2^N P[miss within G] >= A_k
    Gup = best_single_block(B, cost_cap)
    pm_up = P_miss(allowed, Gup, cost_cap, memo)
    upper_ie = base + math.log(pm_up) if (pm_up and pm_up > 0) else None

    core = list(B) if core_cut is None else [q for q in B if q <= core_cut]

    # ln P_T for every subset of core with 1 <= |T| <= rmax (singletons are
    # the exact marginals; |T|>=2 via nested I-E)
    lnP = {frozenset(): 0.0}
    for q in core:
        lnP[frozenset((q,))] = lnp[q]
    skipped = []
    for r in range(2, min(rmax, len(core)) + 1):
        for T in combinations(core, r):
            pm = P_miss(allowed, list(T), cost_cap, memo)
            if pm is None or pm <= 0.0:
                lnP[frozenset(T)] = None
                skipped.append(tuple(T))
            else:
                lnP[frozenset(T)] = math.log(pm)

    # cluster truncations
    trunc = {}
    cluster_contrib = {1: mf_all}
    for r in range(2, rmax + 1):
        if r > len(core):
            break
        s = 0.0
        for T in combinations(core, r):
            cT = cluster_term(T, lnP)
            if cT is not None:
                s += cT
        cluster_contrib[r] = s
    for rr in range(1, rmax + 1):
        tot = base
        for r in range(1, rr + 1):
            tot += cluster_contrib.get(r, 0.0)
        trunc[rr] = tot

    # exact ln A_k via the S519 transfer matrix on the full active set, but
    # ONLY when it is feasible (small k) -- prefixes are nested so we climb
    # and stop at the first abort (never pays the slow full-B abort).
    exact = None
    if want_exact and N <= 40:                 # k <= 80: full B count_tm fits
        last = None
        for i in range(1, len(B) + 1):
            c, st = count_tm(k, list(B[:i]), allowed, max_states=max_states,
                             want_stats=True)
            if c is None:
                last = None
                break
            last = (math.log(c), B[:i])
        if last is not None and last[1] == B:
            exact = last[0]

    return {
        "k": k, "N": N, "B": B, "W": W, "core": core, "base": base,
        "meanfield": meanfield, "block_lower": block_lower, "blocks": blocks,
        "upper": upper_ie, "upper_B": Gup, "trunc": trunc,
        "cluster_contrib": cluster_contrib, "exact": exact, "lnp": lnp,
        "pq": pq, "skipped": skipped,
    }


def ratio(lnval, k):
    return lnval / (k / math.log(k))

# reporting
